Arrive AI launches AP3 Plus with on-device package vision

The delivery endpoint uses Jetson Orin Nano for local package recognition and storage, and the company says it is ready to ship.

Arrive AI / Newswire ↗7 October 2026English editorial summary
StoryImages 1

A new delivery endpoint

Arrive AI introduced AP3 Plus on October 7 and said it was available to ship. The Arrive Point endpoint supports asynchronous parcel exchange by drones, robots, autonomous vehicles or couriers. This product launch is distinct from the later Modovolo partnership, which concerns integrating a particular drone platform.

Recognizing packages and events

An NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano runs vision models to detect package presence, orientation and status, supporting chain-of-custody tracking. Arrive OS handles events such as robot state and door opening or closing. Processing and storage stay on the unit, with optional cloud access and backup according to customer requirements.

Integration still matters

The unit retains its size, connects over cellular or Wi-Fi and uses standard 120-volt power. Arrive says a robot or drone must be able to interface automatically with the opening. Compatibility therefore does not imply zero integration work. The release provides no quantified vision accuracy or handoff-time benchmark.
